title: Interest Rates Are About to DROP… Here’s Where I’m Putting My Money
speaker: Ross Givens

macro_themes.view: Hikes break banks, the Fed's own budget and Treasury interest costs, so the Fed will cut/blink despite 3.4% inflation.
BofA HTM losses likely grew from $82B toward ~$100B with 10-year above 5%; deposit flight risk (SVB playbook).
Short rates fall fastest on cuts; long yields may stay or rise if cuts are seen as bailing out the government.
Rescue paid with a weaker dollar; hard assets win long term.

calls.reason: When the Fed cuts the 2-year yield falls first and fastest; ~5% yield plus price gain (~7% total) with limited risk.
calls.quote: the opportunity, and that I believe is in the two-year Treasury note

calls.reason: Government 'bankrupt'; long yields may stay or rise even if Fed cuts.
calls.quote: Nothing in the world could make me buy a long-term Treasury bond today, ever

calls.reason: Says yields collapse when the Fed blinks, but long-end may not follow and could rise.
calls.quote: Bonds will soar, yields will collapse, and the stock market will rip higher

calls.condition: If the Fed blinks (split vote, dovish remark) at/around the Oct 28 meeting.
calls.reason: Market will read any Fed hesitation as a reversal, ripping stocks higher into midterms.
calls.quote: the stock market will rip higher. Just in time for midterm elections

calls.reason: Weaker dollar from a Fed rescue; expects gold to go exponentially higher in coming years.
calls.quote: Gold is already above 4,000 an ounce. I think it's going exponentially higher in the coming years

calls.reason: Unrealized HTM bond losses (~$100B est.) and deposit flight; Oct 14 earnings could reveal the damage; stock fell ~10% in September.
calls.quote: Something is starting to crack, and we're going to see proof of that on October 14th

notes: Date not stated; '2 weeks after the [Sept 16] hike' suggests ~Sept 30-Oct 1; listing approx 2026-10-02 used. SHY used as ticker for the 2-year note view (outside canonical list). BAC bias is implied, not an explicit trade.
